t:
In this Act:
    (1) Facility.—The term “facility” means any structure, utility, road, or sign constructed on the trust property on or after the date of enactment of this Act. 
    (2) Improvement.—The term “improvement” means—
        (A) a 1,625 square foot 1-story ranch house, built in 1952, located in the SW quarter of sec. 30, T. 17 S., R. 45 W., sixth principal meridian; 
        (B) a 3,600 square foot metal-constructed shop building, built in 1975, located in the SW quarter of sec. 30, T. 17 S., R. 45 W., sixth principal meridian; 
        (C) a livestock corral and shelter; and 
        (D) a water system and wastewater system with all associated utility connections.  
    (3) Secretary.—The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of the Interior. 
    (4) Tribe.—The term “Tribe” means the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes of Oklahoma, a federally recognized Indian tribe. 
    (5) Trust property.—The term “trust property” means the real property, including rights to all minerals, and excluding the improvements, formerly known as the “Dawson Ranch”, consisting of approximately 1,465 total acres presently under the jurisdiction of the Tribe, situated within Kiowa County, Colorado, and more particularly described as follows:
        (A) The portion of sec. 24, T. 17 S., R. 46 W., sixth principal meridian, that is the Eastern half of the NW quarter, the SW quarter of the NE quarter, the NW quarter of the SE quarter, sixth principal meridian. 
        (B) All of sec. 25, T. 17 S., R. 46 W., sixth principal meridian. 
        (C) All of sec. 30, T. 17 S., R. 45 W., sixth principal meridian.

fable.w: This section only defines terms (facility, improvement, Secretary, Tribe, trust property) and describes the land. The tempting reading is that naming an Indian tribe, an entity outside the federal government, signals participation. But the Tribe is only defined here; nothing requires or allows consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body, or a right to sue over any federal decision.
fable.s: means the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes of Oklahoma, a federally recognized Indian tribe

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of definitions for terms used in the Act (e.g., 'Facility', 'Improvement', 'Secretary', 'Tribe', 'Trust property'). It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties before a federal decision is made. It merely defines the scope of property and entities involved.
qwen_block.s: In this Act: (1) Facility.—The term “facility” means any structure, utility, road, or sign constructed on the trust property on or after the date of enactment of this Act.

opus.w: This section only defines terms (facility, improvement, Secretary, Tribe, trust property). It sets up no process for outside parties to take part in a federal decision. The Tribe is named only to define a term, so mentioning a non-federal party is not consultation, coordination, or a right to object or sue.
opus.s: (4) Tribe.—The term “Tribe” means the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes of Oklahoma, a federally recognized Indian tribe.
opus.b:
1. **Tempting reading.** The section names an outside party, the Cheyenne and Arapaho Tribes of Oklahoma, and says the land is "presently under the jurisdiction of the Tribe." That could look like tribal involvement in a federal decision. It fails because this is only a list of definitions. No federal decision is made, and nothing requires the Secretary to consult the Tribe or anyone else, hold a hearing, take comments, set up an advisory body, or allow a lawsuit.

2. **Label.**
